title: Add fast smoke gates tier for batching + cache config diffs (quick feedback before full eval gates)
creator: Talia Benson
content:
Context
Optimize recommendations for batching policy + prefix/KV caching changes are high-frequency and often low-risk, but can still cause correctness/quality issues (esp. long-context, multi-turn chat, and tool/JSON output). Full gates can take too long to run for “one-click apply” and for internal iteration. We need a fast tier (“smoke gate”) that gives quick feedback and blocks obviously unsafe changes, before scheduling more expensive full gates.

Goal
Implement a smoke gate tier for batching + cache config diffs that:
- Runs quickly (minutes, not hours)
- Has bounded cost
- Uses a small but high-signal prompt subset with minimum coverage rules
- Produces pass/fail + reasons in the same gate-run state machine used by Optimize
- Has a retry policy that reduces false negatives due to infra flakes

Non-goals (v0)
- Smoke gates for quantization profile changes (handled by ENG-3924)
- Replacing the full gate tier (smoke is additive, not sufficient by itself for higher-risk diffs)
- Perfect statistical confidence; smoke gates are primarily a “tripwire”

Scope
1) New gate tier type
- Add “SMOKE” tier to the gate policy model and gate-run schema (if not already present).
- Tier applies to config diff types:
  - Batching policy updates (continuous batching params, max batch tokens, scheduling params)
  - Prefix cache enable/disable + sizing/eviction settings
  - KV cache behavior settings exposed through Optimize (e.g., cache reuse thresholds where applicable)

2) Prompt subset selection
- Define a fixed “smoke prompt set” per model family (initially: Llama-3.x instruct variants and the top 2 Redwood-verified models used in hosted API).
- Prompt subset requirements (MVP):
  - Minimum 40 prompts per model family, stratified:
    - 15 chat multi-turn prompts (>= 3 turns)
    - 10 long-context prompts (>= 8k tokens total input when rendered; can be synthetic)
    - 10 structured output prompts (JSON schema / tool calling style)
    - 5 “known hard cases” tagged by Applied ML (regression-prone)
  - Must include at least 3 prompts that force streaming responses (to catch chunking/stop sequence behavior changes)
  - Must include at least 5 prompts with system + developer role + user role ordering (to catch formatting regressions)

Note: Prompt set ownership/curation lives with Applied ML (Jonas/Karthik/Selene). This ticket implements the tier mechanics + selection plumbing, and consumes the prompt set IDs.

3) Target runtime + SLA
- Target wall-clock runtime per smoke gate run:
  - p50 <= 6 minutes
  - p95 <= 12 minutes
- Hard timeout: 20 minutes (mark as “FAILED_INFRA_TIMEOUT” rather than quality fail)
- Concurrency limits: respect eval-harness limits and GPU availability (do not starve full gate queue).

4) Pass/fail rules (smoke tier)
- Smoke tier should be intentionally conservative for “obvious breakage”, not sensitive to small deltas.
- Base pass/fail:
  - Task success rate delta must be >= -2.0% absolute vs baseline on smoke suite OR must satisfy “no critical failures” rule below.
  - “Critical failures” are defined as any of:
    - Structured output invalid JSON rate increases by >= +3.0% absolute
    - Tool-call format mismatch rate increases by >= +3.0% absolute
    - Empty/aborted generation rate increases by >= +2.0% absolute
    - Repetition/degenerate output heuristic triggers increases by >= +5.0% absolute
  - If any critical failure rule triggers: FAIL (no override-by-retry).

Baseline
- Use the baseline selection mechanism from the main gating system:
  - Same model version + current prod config for the route/account
  - If route has no baseline snapshots, fall back to Redwood “default config” baseline for that model family + hardware SKU

5) Retry + flake handling
- Retries are for infra flakiness, not “quality flakiness.”
- Retry policy (smoke tier):
  - Automatic retry up to 1 time if failure reason is in:
    - TIMEOUT_INFRA
    - GPU_OOM (only if OOM is in eval job runner, not in model execution correctness)
    - TRANSIENT_5XX from eval-harness
  - No automatic retry for deterministic “quality fail” reasons.
  - If rerun passes after infra failure: mark final status as PASSED with a “rerun_required=true” flag in artifacts/summary.
- If repeated infra failures occur (2 attempts both infra fail): mark as FAILED_INFRA and surface as “gate could not be evaluated” (blocks apply by default).

6) Integration points
- Optimize service
  - When a batching/cache diff is proposed (recommendation preview or apply), run smoke gate immediately.
  - Smoke gate result should be shown in Console alongside full gate status.
  - Policy: for self-serve routes, smoke gate must pass before “Run full gates” button is enabled (reduces wasted spend on doomed diffs).
  - For auto-apply workflows: smoke gate must pass before canary begins.
- Eval-harness
  - Use the trigger API from ENG-3922.
  - Ensure request includes: tier=SMOKE, prompt_set_id(s), config diff, baseline config pointer.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New SMOKE gate tier is supported end-to-end: Optimize -> eval-harness -> results ingested -> state machine updated
- [ ] For batching/cache diffs, a smoke gate is automatically created and started within 30s of proposal creation (excluding queue delay)
- [ ] p50 runtime <= 6 min and p95 <= 12 min for internal beta routes over a 7-day window
- [ ] Retry behavior matches policy; infra failure vs quality failure are clearly separated in status + UI reason code
- [ ] Minimum coverage rules enforced (fails with “INVALID_PROMPT_SET_COVERAGE” if prompt set doesn’t meet requirements)
- [ ] Emits observability signals (at least): gate_duration_seconds, gate_attempts, gate_status, gate_failure_reason, tier=smoke, config_type

Implementation plan (engineering)
1) Schema/policy
- Add gate_tier=SMOKE to enums used by Optimize service and persisted gate-run records.
- Add a per-config-type policy mapping:
  - batching/cache => run_smoke=true, run_full=true (full may be deferred until smoke pass)

2) Prompt set resolution
- Add lookup in Optimize gating config:
  - model_family -> smoke_prompt_set_id
- Add validation step:
  - Query eval-harness prompt set metadata and ensure category counts meet minimum coverage.

3) Trigger + orchestration
- New “smoke gate runner” path that calls eval-harness with:
  - suite=smoke
  - strict smaller max prompts cap
  - reduced sampling (no multiple seeds) unless required for determinism

4) Result interpretation
- Implement smoke-tier scoring + critical failure checks.
- Ensure reason codes are stable and mapped to Console copy.

5) Observability
- Add metrics tags: tier=smoke, config_type=batching|cache, model_family, region.
- Add tracing span around:
  - prompt set resolution
  - eval-harness trigger
  - result ingest

Open questions
- Should smoke gates be mandatory for “manual config changes” outside Optimize (future: hook into config change pipeline)? For now: only Optimize paths.
- Do we want to allow full gates to run in parallel with smoke gates for enterprise routes (to reduce time-to-deploy), while still blocking apply until smoke passes?
- How do we handle long-context synthetic prompts across models with different context windows? (Need a per-model context ceiling.)

Risks / notes
- Smoke suite can become noisy if prompt set isn’t curated (ties to ENG-3929 flake detection + quarantine workflow).
- GPU scarcity may violate runtime SLO even if suite is small; we may need a dedicated small queue with preemptible capacity.
- Some batching/cache diffs may affect latency but not quality; smoke gates should not include latency as pass/fail criteria (handled separately via rollout SLOs).

- System design: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimize-quality-gates-system-design.json
- Metrics/thresholds: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/quality-gate-metrics-and-thresholds-v1.json

Updates / comments
2025-12-03 (Olivia Grant)
- Synced with Jonas/Karthik: initial smoke suite will prioritize structured output + long-context because those are most sensitive to cache behavior. They’ll provide prompt_set_id list by 12/10.
- Agreed that smoke gate FAIL should block full gate launch for self-serve to avoid spend.

2025-12-12 (Sofia Ivanova)
- Flag: some “batching policy” knobs can change EOS/stop-sequence timing under streaming if max_tokens_per_step changes. Recommend adding at least 3 streaming prompts with explicit stop sequences.

2026-01-08 (Olivia Grant)
- Implemented tier plumbing in Optimize behind feature flag optimize_gates_smoke_tier.
- Still missing: prompt set metadata validation call (waiting on eval-harness metadata endpoint shape; temporary hardcoded counts).

2026-01-15 (Sean Gallagher)
- Request: add metric for “gate_queue_delay_seconds” to separate eval runtime from scheduling delay; otherwise p95 will look bad during GPU pressure.

2026-01-22 (Olivia Grant)
- Added retry logic for TIMEOUT_INFRA + TRANSIENT_5XX; no retry for quality fail.
- Next: wire critical failure checks (invalid JSON / tool format) based on eval-harness outputs; need confirmation on exact field names from ENG-3922.
